snapshot.central_hypothesis: If spherically symmetric stellar collapse satisfies AANEC, global hyperbolicity, regular matter fields, complete null generators, and an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition, then reaching a model-dependent compactness threshold forces trapped-surface formation; consequently, stable non-black-hole remnants above a compactness-dependent mass scale are excluded within this restricted model class. This does not by itself explain the observed 2-5 solar mass gap, which may be governed by supernova explosion physics, fallback, equation-of-state uncertainties, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, or binary interactions.
snapshot.claim_scope: Formal theorem/conjecture for classical GR, spherical nonrotating collapse with isotropic pressure, regular matter fields, global hyperbolicity, complete null generators, AANEC, and an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition. Not a quantitative derivation of the observed 2-5 solar mass gap, not a general proof that all massive stars necessarily form black holes, and not a replacement for stellar-evolution or supernova-engine explanations.
snapshot.mechanism_or_relation: Replace pointwise NEC/SEC assumptions with AANEC plus an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing assumption on null congruence generators; derive a trapped-surface threshold via Raychaudhuri-type focusing and Misner-Sharp compactness, then bound stable non-black-hole remnants through TOV-like stellar-structure assumptions. The observed mass gap is treated as an astrophysical consistency constraint, with alternative stellar-physics mechanisms identified as confounders.

snapshot.title: A Qualified AANEC Trapped-Surface Bound for Non-Black-Hole Stellar Remnants

assumptions: Spherically symmetric collapse of massive stars with isotropic pressure.
Matter fields satisfy AANEC along complete null generators and do not exhibit uncontrolled quantum ANEC violations.
Spacetime is globally hyperbolic and sufficiently regular for trapped-surface arguments.
An explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition holds along the relevant generators; this is an independent geometric hypothesis, not a consequence of AANEC alone.
Non-black-hole remnants are modeled as stable equilibrium objects obeying a bounded compactness or TOV-like limit.
The observed 2-5 solar mass gap is not assumed to be a direct consequence of the theorem; it is treated as an astrophysical consistency constraint subject to alternative stellar-physics explanations.
hypothesis.boundary_or_failure_condition: The theorem fails or must be restricted if AANEC is violated, the added averaged null-convergence/focusing condition fails, null generators are incomplete, quantum stress-energy violates ANEC, nonspherical/rotating/magnetic dynamics dominate, or stable exotic compact objects evade the averaged-focusing assumptions. The mass-gap inference fails or becomes non-discriminating if explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, pair-instability processes, or binary evolution dominate the observed remnant distribution.
hypothesis.central_hypothesis: If spherically symmetric stellar collapse satisfies AANEC, global hyperbolicity, regular matter fields, complete null generators, and an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition, then reaching a model-dependent compactness threshold forces trapped-surface formation; consequently, stable non-black-hole remnants above a compactness-dependent mass scale are excluded within this restricted model class. This does not by itself explain the observed 2-5 solar mass gap, which may be governed by supernova explosion physics, fallback, equation-of-state uncertainties, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, or binary interactions.

hypothesis.discriminating_observation: A rigorous proof or counterexample distinguishing whether AANEC plus explicit averaged focusing yields a trapped-surface/compactness bound; astrophysical observations of the mass gap alone are not sufficient to distinguish the theorem from explosion, fallback, equation-of-state, rotation, magnetic-field, nonspherical, or binary-evolution explanations.
evidence_basis: SURVEY_ANCHOR: realistic matter fields may violate SEC while satisfying DEC, motivating relaxation of pointwise energy conditions.
SURVEY_ANCHOR: observed mass gap is a discriminator for supernova engine physics, implying it is astrophysically inferred rather than a pure GR theorem.

Uncertainty note: AANEC alone may not imply the local or integrated focusing needed for Penrose-type trapped-surface formation; the added averaged null-convergence/focusing condition is therefore essential but may be as restrictive as the original pointwise assumption in some regimes.
Uncertainty note: stellar remnant masses are sensitive to explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, and binary interactions.
hypothesis.evidence_requirement: A proof or counterexample establishing whether AANEC plus the stated averaged null-convergence/focusing and stellar-structure assumptions implies a trapped-surface/compactness bound. Separately, astrophysical inference is required to connect any bound to the observed mass gap; the observed gap alone cannot distinguish the theorem from explosion, fallback, equation-of-state, rotation, magnetic-field, nonspherical, or binary-evolution explanations.
hypothesis.expected_mechanism: AANEC plus explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing forces relevant null congruences to converge sufficiently to form a trapped surface when compactness exceeds a model-dependent threshold; this excludes stable non-black-hole remnants above a compactness-dependent mass scale within the restricted theorem class.
hypothesis.intervention_or_transformation: Relax pointwise NEC/SEC to AANEC and add an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition to the trapped-surface theorem, while demoting the observed stellar mass gap to an astrophysical consistency constraint rather than a theorem-derived prediction.
